_note: English Booklet A answers read off the scan by eye, for the cells the grid
reader in build/en_key.py refused. Committed because work-en-ans/ is
regenerated; the precedent is review/prelim-mcq-key.json, which does the same
job for the two Science schools that printed their key as a picture.
These are NOT a substitute for reading the page. build/en_key.py checks every
entry here against every cell the scan could establish and fails the
extraction outright if the two disagree, so this file can fill gaps but can
never quietly overrule the scan. See CLAUDE.md section 1.6.1 for why a wrong
digit here is the worst failure in the project: there is no partial credit to
soften it, and the child is simply told they were wrong when they were right.
2026-prelim-nanyang: the grid reader read 22 of 25 cells unaided and agrees
with the eye reading on every one of them. The three below are cells where
the readings did not reach agreement, not cells where they conflicted; each
was read twice from the 300 dpi render, magnified.
2025-prelim-nanyang: a different table layout from 2026's (typeset, not
handwritten-grid; four tables rather than the ruled-digit-cell shape
en_key.py's geometry reader was tuned against), so it read only 10 of 25
cells unaided. The other 15 are read by eye from the same 300 dpi render, at
full resolution. All 25 are listed here rather than just the gaps, and the 10
the reader did establish agree with the eye reading on every one -- see
work-en-ans/2025-prelim-nanyang/mcq-answers.json before this file was added.
The nine 2026-prelim schools ingested alongside Nanyang (ACSJ, Ai Tong, CHIJ
OLGS, Nan Hua, PLMGS, Raffles, Red Swastika, St Nicholas, Tao Nan) all use a
third layout again: one wide ruled table of Q-number *rows* (a header row of
Q1..Q10 etc, the answer row directly beneath it) rather than 2025-Nanyang's
alternating question/answer *columns* -- find_tables()/read_grid() in
en_key.py were tuned against the column-pair shape and find zero tables on
this one, so all 25 of each are read by eye rather than left to a reader
that cannot see the geometry at all. Eight of the nine share one source
template (a heavy 'sgexam.com'/'testpaper.com' watermark, white text
printing through its black shapes as a legible cutout -- the same effect
CLAUDE.md section 12.2 records for the Chinese prelim keys); CHIJ OLGS uses
the school's own plainer Question/Answer-column template with only a light,
non-obscuring diagonal watermark. Every cell on every one of the nine was
read at 2-3x zoom and cross-checked against the page's own OCR text where the
watermark did not interfere; none disagreed.
St Nicholas's Answer key PDF carries a stray extra page at the front -- page
1 is actually the tail end of the question booklet (Q73-75, 'END OF PAPER'),
not part of the key at all -- so its grid is on page-002.png, not page-001.png
as for the other eight. A one-off filing slip in the source, not a format
difference; build/en_key.py's booklet_bands() already searches every page for
a 'BOOKLET A' heading rather than assuming page 1, so this needs no code
change, only noting here in case work-en-ans/ is ever rebuilt and the page
count looks wrong at a glance.

2026-prelim-st-nicholas.read: by eye from work-en-ans/2026-prelim-st-nicholas/pages/page-002.png (page-001.png is a stray question-booklet page, see _note)
